tagline: Down both shores of a shallow lagoon, rockets to the east.
intro: From just north of Titusville the byway runs south in two strands, US 1 on the mainland through Titusville, Cocoa, Melbourne and Sebastian, and A1A on the barrier island through Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach to Wabasso Beach, with causeways between them. The lagoon is half a mile to five miles wide and averages four feet deep. Before the railroad came, it was the road.

Local history says Titusville got its name from a game of dominoes. The Kennedy Space Center lies to the east of it. South of Melbourne Beach, A1A runs twenty miles beside a refuge where about a quarter of the sea turtles nesting in the United States come ashore.

moments.title: Cocoa
moments.text: The mail once came by riverboat, and one story says it was left in a Baker's Cocoa tin nailed to a piling, which named the town. Travis Hardware has been open since 1885.

moments.title: McLarty Treasure Museum
moments.text: Survivors of the 1715 Spanish treasure fleet camped here after a hurricane wrecked it. A museum on the site keeps artifacts from the wreck and a deck looking out on the Atlantic.

moments.title: Pelican Island
moments.text: A three-acre island in the lagoon that Theodore Roosevelt made the first national wildlife refuge in 1903, to keep its birds from the plume hunters who supplied ladies' hats.
